# ai-plc-prototype-build scope

Standard depth for the third AI-PLC entry point: the workspace already holds
`PROTOTYPE-*.md` specification files (generated by an earlier
`ai-plc` run, possibly by a different team), so all discovery is
skipped and the run goes straight to building the prototypes, then continues
to product strategy, go-to-market, and the Discovery Document. This is the
workshop/distributed-team pattern: a core group runs discovery once,
distributes the portable spec files, and each receiving team builds under
this scope.

## Why these stages, why skip those

Unlike the runtime fork between the pain-point and use-case entry points
(which share `ai-plc` because a PR/FAQ can merge into the use-case
path mid-run), "the specs already exist" is knowable before the workflow
starts - so it is a scope decision, not a stage condition. Envision, solution
analysis, use-case intake, prioritization, and prototype-context generation
are SKIP: their outputs are embodied in the spec files this scope starts
from. Prototype building, product strategy, go-to-market, and the Discovery
Document assembly execute.

## Membership

Keyword triggers: `build prototypes`, `prototype specs`,
`prototype from spec`. `ai-plc-prototype-building`, `ai-plc-product-strategy`,
`ai-plc-go-to-market`, and `ai-plc-discovery-document` execute;
initialization always executes; the five upstream discovery stages and every
core phase stage are SKIP.
